messages:
maria: Quick follow-up to the iterator/transport RFC — I'm still fuzzy on who owns what for pagination retries. Link to RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/transport-retries
kevin: My gut: keep transport-layer retries for idempotent unary calls only. For paginated/streaming we need SDK-level resume that knows cursor semantics.
jen: Agree. Also: different language ergonomics matter. Python generator vs TS async iterator vs Go channel — want the same guarantees but different APIs.
oscar: Production note: if transport auto-retries a paged request we might double-charge customers if we re-run an expensive backend op. Need a safe-idempotency signal.
maria: How would that signal look? header? rpc option? example?
kevin: Could be a boolean "accept_non_idempotent_retry" or an idempotency token. But tokens require server support.
jen: SDK-level approach idea:
```
// TS pseudo
for await (const page of client.listItems({ pageSize: 100 })) {
  // client handles resume tokens & incremental backoff
}
```
SDK keeps cursor, applies exponential backoff, switches transport endpoints if needed.
oscar: +1. Also recommend exposing hooks: onRetry, onResume, so platform teams can instrument per-customer token costs.
deploy-bot: canary deploy succeeded: transport-retries v0.3 -> infra-prod
maria: Tradeoff: if SDK owns backoff, it may duplicate logic across languages. But we can centralize heuristics in a shared lib (go/python/ts implement thin shims) — thoughts?
kevin: We should separate two orthogonal concerns: 1) failure handling policy (backoff windows, max attempts) 2) resume semantics (cursor merger, dedupe). Policy can be a small crosslang JSON config; resume is language-specific code.
jen: For TS/Python we can provide the high-level iterator that uses the policy config. In Go, provide a streaming client with context-aware Resume(ctx) return.
oscar: Edge case: partially-consumed pages (client aborted mid-page). We need a deterministic resume token on server side, or the SDK must re-request previous page and drop seen items (requires stable item ids).
maria: Implementation checklist:
- Add `retryPolicy` config to SDK ctor (maxAttempts, initialBackoff, jitter)
- Transport default: no retries for paginated/streaming unless explicit idempotent flag
- SDK: store lastCursor, replay from cursor on retry; expose onRetry/onResume hooks
- Docs: examples for Python/TS/Go
jen: Also add integration tests that simulate transient errors at Nth page to validate resume correctness.
kevin: One more: for streaming (gRPC/HTTP2) we may prefer windowed reconnect vs cursor replay — document tradeoffs.
maria: OK I'll draft a follow-up RFC section with the checklist + proposed config schema and ping infra for server-side idempotency token support.
oscar: Thanks — happy to pair on the integration tests. :thumbsup:
